subject.summary: The Members page in Fieldnote's workspace settings, where admins invite people, change roles and remove access a few times a month.

theme.summary: Light theme; Inter at 14px body; slate neutrals with an indigo accent used only for primary actions; 8px radius; hairline borders; calm, plain-spoken copy.

must_keep: See every member with name, email, role and last active date
Search members by name or email
Filter by role: Owner, Admin, Member, Guest
Invite people by email with a role, validated
Change a member's role (the Owner role cannot be removed from the last owner)
Resend or revoke a pending invite
Seat usage: used of available seats
Fieldnote brand: indigo for primary actions only, Inter, calm copy
constraints: Desktop web at 1280×800, usable at 390 wide

baseline.name: Today
baseline.description: The Members page as it ships now: a table with a role filter, search, an Invite dialog and row menus.

preferences.why: Picked 1h, then chose 2a, which keeps its role cards.

preferences.trait: a command bar as the main way to act

rounds.question: How should admins see and manage who has access?
rounds.title: Ten ways to manage who has access
rounds.summary: All ten use the same 24 members and 3 pending invites, and keep search, role filtering, inviting, role changes, removal with confirmation, invite resend and the seat count. Every frame is live; Invite, role changes and removal work. Emails are not actually sent.

rounds.question: How far can role cards with a filter rail go?
rounds.title: Five takes on role cards with a filter rail
rounds.summary: Five variations of 2a, from a sharper version of it to a wildcard that drops the role cards. All five use the same 24 members and 3 pending invites and keep every must-keep function; 3d crosses 2a with 1j's review queue.
rounds.feedback: More like 2a, please. No command bar. Five is enough, and include one wild one.
